<section class="block" id="finding" aria-labelledby="h-finding">
  <div class="wrap grid2">
    <div>
      <h2 id="h-finding">The finding</h2>
      <p class="q">Can you tell whether a first-order logic translation says what its sentence says, without a gold formula?</p>
      <p>Gold references for <button class="term" data-term="nlfol">NL→FOL</button> are expensive, and audits find that roughly 40% of benchmark annotations contain errors. The paper tests a gold-free alternative. Ask several independent LLM families to translate the same sentence, check with the Z3 solver which of their formulas are logically equivalent to the candidate, and score the candidate by the share of <button class="term" data-term="peer">cross-family peers</button> that disagree with it. That score is <button class="term" data-term="calign">c_score_align</button>.</p>
      <p>On the development set it separates faithful translations from errors better than cheap API judges: <button class="term" data-term="strat">stratified AUROC</button> 0.741 against 0.642 for the <button class="term" data-term="disg">disguised</button> flash-lite judge.</p>
      <div class="big" aria-hidden="true">+0.099</div>
      <p class="big-cap">AUROC gain over the disguised flash-lite judge on the <button class="term" data-term="rab">R_AB</button> population, 95% CI [+0.049, +0.146].</p>
      <p>The answer comes with a hard caveat. Confirmation on fresh data failed: every fresh-data cell was either not testable or unfavourable. The metric also raises false alarms on meaning-preserving renames, and its power falls with sentence length. Read it as a preliminary lead.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="card">
      <p class="q" id="q-head">Does the advantage hold in every kind of sentence?</p>
      <div class="controls">
        <div class="seg" role="group" aria-label="Population" id="pop-seg"></div>
      </div>
      <div class="controls" role="group" aria-label="Metric groups shown" id="grp-ck"></div>
      <div class="chart" id="chart-head" aria-describedby="q-head"></div>
      <div class="legend" id="leg-head"></div>
      <p class="takeaway" id="tk-head" aria-live="polite"></p>
      <p class="small">Bars are computed in the page from the 2,686 recorded per-item scores (higher score = more likely unfaithful). Whiskers are the recorded 95% sentence-cluster bootstrap CIs, shown for the full population only. The flash-lite disguised judge is always drawn as the baseline.</p>
    </div>
  </div>
</section>

Verdicts use the two thresholds set in <a href="#try">Try it</a> (default 0.50 for both).</p>

        <p class="small">Correct base formulas were rewritten with <button class="term" data-term="rename">meaning-preserving renames</button>. A metric should not care. Grey is the <button class="term" data-term="fa">false-alarm</button> rate on the unrenamed bases, colour the rate after the rename; the gap is the <button class="term" data-term="flip">flip</button>.</p>
        <div class="seg" role="group" aria-label="Rename type" id="ren-seg"></div>
        <div class="chart" id="chart-ren" style="margin-top:10px"></div>
        <div class="legend"><span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--gray)"></i>Base FA</span><span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--accent)"></i>FA after rename (consensus)</span><span><i class="sw" style="background:var(--base)"></i>FA after rename (other)</span></div>
        <p class="takeaway" id="tk-ren" aria-live="polite"></p>
      </div>
      <div>
        <h3>Errors the peers share</h3>
        <p class="q">Which kinds of error slip past the consensus?</p>
        <p class="small">Recall per error group with every metric's threshold set so that 10% of correct R_AB items are flagged. Compare the consensus with another metric.</p>
        <label class="fld">Compare c_score_align with<select id="grp-cmp"></select></label>
        <div class="chart" id="chart-grp" style="margin-top:10px"></div>
        <div class="legend" id="leg-grp"></div>
        <p class="takeaway" id="tk-grp" aria-live="polite"></p>
      </div>
    </div>

    <h3 style="margin-top:40px">The confirmation attempt</h3>
    <p class="q prose">Did the development-set advantage survive on fresh data?</p>
    <div class="tscroll"><table id="conf-table"></table></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-conf"></p>

    <h3 style="margin-top:36px">What the paper does not show</h3>
    <ul class="plain prose">
      <li><strong>Development data only.</strong> Every positive result in the main table is on data used to design the metric. The confirmation attempt produced no testable positive cell.</li>
      <li><strong>Rename vulnerability.</strong> A 76.5% false-alarm rate on nonce renames means the metric will penalise translations with non-standard predicate names, even when they are correct.</li>
      <li><strong>Length degradation.</strong> Discrimination falls with sentence length (NET +0.356), driven by correct-translation divergence. The metric is weakest on the longest sentences, where gold-free evaluation is most needed.</li>
      <li><strong>Label dependence.</strong> All development results rest on panel labels whose agreement is imperfect; part of the advantage could reflect agreement with panel biases.</li>
      <li><strong>Cost.</strong> Cheaper than a frontier judge, but it needs k peer translations per sentence: $0.95 per 1,000 sentences at k = 3.</li>
      <li><strong>Domain.</strong> English→FOL from MALLS and ProverQA only. Other formalisms, languages and sentence distributions are untested.</li>
    </ul>
  </div>
</section>

The paper tests a gold-free alternative. Ask several independent LLM families to translate the same sentence, check with the Z3 solver which of their formulas are logically equivalent to the candidate, and score the candidate by the share of <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"peer\">cross-family peers</button> that disagree with it. That score is <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"calign\">c_score_align</button>.</p>\n      <p>On the development set it separates faithful translations from errors better than cheap API judges: <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"strat\">stratified AUROC</button> 0.741 against 0.642 for the <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"disg\">disguised</button> flash-lite judge.</p>\n      <div class=\"big\" aria-hidden=\"true\">+0.099</div>\n      <p class=\"big-cap\">AUROC gain over the disguised flash-lite judge on the <button class=\"term\" data-term=\"rab\">R_AB</button> population, 95% CI [+0.049, +0.146].</p>\n      <p>The answer comes with a hard caveat. Confirmation on fresh data failed: every fresh-data cell was either not testable or unfavourable. The metric also raises false alarms on meaning-preserving renames, and its power falls with sentence length.     <div><h4>What happens</h4><p>Nothing is parsed yet. The metric receives only the sentence and the candidate. No gold formula, ontology or vocabulary is supplied.</p></div>
    <div><h4>Out</h4><p>The sentence is sent to ${fams.length} LLM families with one frozen few-shot prompt.</p><p class="small">Reference formula, used only to label candidates for this evaluation:</p><code class="fol">${esc(ex.ref)}</code></div></div>`;
  } else if (i === 1) {
    h += `<p>Each family translates independently. ${rows.filter(r => r.peer).length} parseable peer outputs; ${ex.unparseable.length} unparseable output(s) are counted, not scored. Identical formulas share a label F1…F${ex.nodes.length}.</p><div class="tscroll"><table><thead><tr><th>Family</th><th>System</th><th>Formula</th><th>Panel label</th></tr></thead><tbody>` +
      rows.map(r => `<tr><td>${esc(r.peer ? r.fam : 'gold (never a peer)')}</td><td class="small">${esc(r.sys.replace(/^G\d+b?:/, ''))}</td><td><b>F${r.node + 1}</b> <code class="fol">${esc(ex.nodes[r.node].fol)}</code></td><td>${r.peer ? tagOf(r.label) : '<span class="small">reference</span>'}</td></tr>`).join('') +
      `</tbody></table></div><p class="small">Why several families: models from different vendors rarely make the same mistake, so a wrong formula tends to stand alone.</p>`;
  } else if (i === 2) {
    h += `<div class="io" style="grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,1.3fr)"><div>${miniGraph(ex, cand.node)}<p class="small">Solid teal: equal after canonicalisation. Solid blue: equivalent after predicate alignment. Dashed orange: equivalent after a granularity bridge. Red ring: holds an ERROR row.</p></div>
    <div>${candSel}<p style="margin-top:10px">Candidate <b>F${cand.node + 1}</b>: <code class="fol">${esc(fol)}</code></p><p>Families name predicates differently, so the aligner searches cheap one-to-one predicate maps before Z3 checks equivalence. A pair counts as equivalent if any map yields a Z3-verified equivalence.</p>
    <div class="tscroll"><table><thead><tr><th>Peer</th><th>Formula</th><th>Z3 verdict vs candidate</th></tr></thead><tbody>${S.det.map(d => `<tr><td>${esc(d.p.fam)}</td><td>F${d.p.node + 1}</td><td>${d.eq ? `<span class="eqy">equivalent</span> <span class="small">(${d.eq === 'same' ? 'same formula' : d.eq})</span>` : '<span class="eqn">not equivalent</span>'}</td></tr>`).join('')}</tbody></table></div></div></div>`;
  } else if (i === 3) {
    const ok = S.c != null && cand.c != null && Math.abs(S.c - cand.c) < 5e-4;
    h += `${candSel}<div class="io" style="margin-top:12px"><div><h4>In</h4><p>${S.n} peer outputs from families other than ${esc(cand.fam)} (its own family is excluded).</p></div>
    <div><h4>What happens</h4><p>c_score_align = 1 − (equivalent peers) / (peers)</p><p class="num" style="font-size:1.15rem">= 1 − ${S.nEq} / ${S.n} = <b>${f3(S.c)}</b></p></div>
    <div><h4>Out</h4><p>Higher means more peers disagree, so the candidate is more likely unfaithful.</p><p class="small">Computed here from the recorded solver verdicts; the recorded score in the run is ${f3(cand.c)}${ok ? ', an exact match' : ''}.</p></div></div>`;
  } else {
    const lab = rows.filter(r => r.rab).map(r => Object.assign({ cs: exScore(ex, r.k).c }, r)).sort((a, b) => b.cs - a.cs);
    h += `<p>All labelled candidates of this sentence ranked by consensus score, beside the recorded disguised flash-lite judge score (probability of unfaithful, 0 to 1).</p><div class="tscroll"><table><thead><tr><th>System</th><th>Formula</th><th>c_score_align</th><th>Judge</th><th>Panel label</th></tr></thead><tbody>` +
      lab.map(r => `<tr style="${r.k === SS.cand ? 'background:#e3ecf8' : ''}"><td class="small">${esc(r.sys.replace(/^G\d+b?:/, ''))}</td><td>F${r.node + 1}</td><td class="num">${f3(r.cs)}</td><td class="num">${f2(r.j)}</td><td>${tagOf(r.label)} <span class="small">${esc((r.ops || []).join(', '))}</span></td></tr>`).join('') + `</tbody></table></div>`;
  }
  $('#stage-body').innerHTML = h;
  const cs = $('#cand-sel'); if (cs) cs.addEventListener('change', e => { SS.cand = e.target.value; drawStage(false); const n = $('#cand-sel'); if (n) n.focus(); });
  if (announce) $('#stage-live').textContent = `Stage ${i + 1} of ${STAGES.length}: ${STAGES[i].short}`;
  // takeaway
  const lab = rows.filter(r => r.rab).map(r => ({ r, c: exScore(ex, r.k).c }));
  const errs = lab.filter(x => x.r.label === 'ERROR'), cors = lab.filter(x => x.r.label === 'CORRECT');
  const me = (a) => a.length ? a.reduce((s, x) => s + x.c, 0) / a.length : NaN;
  const jFa = cors.filter(x => x.r.j >= 0.5).length;
  let t = `Candidate ${cand.sys.replace(/^G\d+b?:/, '')} (${cand.label}) scores ${f3(S.c)}. Across this sentence, ERROR candidates average ${f3(me(errs))} and CORRECT candidates ${f3(me(cors))}; the judge rates ${jFa} of ${cors.length} correct candidates at 0.5 or above.`;
  if (me(errs) < me(cors)) t += ' Here the errors agree with most peers, so the consensus ranks them as safer than the correct translations.';
  else t += ' Correct translations cluster; the errors stand apart.';
  $('#tk-step').textContent = t;
}

/* ---------- global thresholds ---------- */
const TH = { c: 0.5, j: 0.5 };
const flagC = r => sc(r, 'c_score_align') >= TH.c - 1e-9;
const flagJ = r => sc(r, 'judge_cheap_disg') >= TH.j - 1e-9;

/* ---------- 3a. item browser ---------- */
const BS = { st: 'all', y: 'all', cs: 'all', sort: 'cdesc', q: '', shown: 60, sel: null };
function initBrowser() {
  const st = $('#f-st'); st.innerHTML = '<option value="all">All strata</option>' + ['L25', 'L20', 'EXC', 'CTRL'].map(s => `<option value="${s}">${POPS[s].label}</option>`).join('');
  st.addEventListener('change', e => { BS.st = e.target.value; BS.shown = 60; drawBrowser(); });
  $('#f-y').addEventListener('change', e => { BS.y = e.target.value; BS.shown = 60; drawBrowser(); });
  $('#f-case').addEventListener('change', e => { BS.cs = e.target.value; BS.shown = 60; drawBrowser(); });
  $('#f-sort').addEventListener('change', e => { BS.sort = e.target.value; drawBrowser(); });
  let tmo; $('#f-q').addEventListener('input', e => { clearTimeout(tmo); tmo = setTimeout(() => { BS.q = e.target.value.trim().toLowerCase(); BS.shown = 60; drawBrowser(); }, 150); });
  $('#b-more').addEventListener('click', () => { BS.shown += 60; drawBrowser(); });
}
function caseOk(r) {
  const c = flagC(r), j = flagJ(r);
  switch (BS.cs) {
    case 'cwin': return r.y ? (c && !j) : (!c && j);
    case 'jwin': return r.y ? (j && !c) : (!j && c);
    case 'miss': return r.y === 1 && !c;
    case 'fa': return r.y === 0 && c;
    default: return true;
  }
}
function filtered() {
  const q = BS.q;
  let out = ROWS.filter(r => (BS.st === 'all' || r.st === BS.st) && (BS.y === 'all' || String(r.y) === BS.y) && caseOk(r) &&
    (!q || SENT[r.s].text.toLowerCase().includes(q) || r.fol.toLowerCase().includes(q) || r.sys.toLowerCase().includes(q) || r.fam.toLowerCase().includes(q)));
  const key = { cdesc: r => -sc(r, 'c_score_align'), casc: r => sc(r, 'c_score_align'), wdesc: r => -r.w, jdesc: r => -sc(r, 'judge_cheap_disg') }[BS.sort];
  out = out.map((r, i) => [key(r), i, r]).sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0] || a[1] - b[1]).map(x => x[2]);
  return out;
}
function drawBrowser() {
  const list = filtered(), ul = $('#b-list');
  const nE = list.filter(r => r.y).length;
  $('#b-count').textContent = `${list.length} of ${ROWS.length} candidates match (${nE} ERROR, ${list.length - nE} CORRECT). Showing ${Math.min(BS.shown, list.length)}.`;
  ul.innerHTML = '';
  if (!list.length) ul.innerHTML = '<li style="padding:14px" class="small">No candidate matches these filters.</li>';
  list.slice(0, BS.shown).forEach(r => {
    const li = document.createElement('li'), b = document.createElement('button');
    b.type = 'button'; b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', r === BS.sel);
    const t = SENT[r.s].text;
    b.innerHTML = `<div>${esc(t.length > 110 ? t.slice(0, 107) + '…' : t)}</div><div class="meta">${tagOf(r.y ? 'ERROR' : 'CORRECT')}<span>c ${f3(sc(r, 'c_score_align'))}</span><span>judge ${f2(sc(r, 'judge_cheap_disg'))}</span><span>${esc(r.sys.replace(/^G\d+b?:/, '').split('/').pop())}</span><span>${r.st}</span></div>`;
    b.addEventListener('click', () => { BS.sel = r; $$('button', ul).forEach(x => x.setAttribute('aria-pressed', 'false')); b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', 'true'); drawDetail(); });
    li.appendChild(b); ul.appendChild(li);
  });
  $('#b-more').disabled = BS.shown >= list.length;
  if (!BS.sel || !list.includes(BS.sel)) { BS.sel = list[0] || null; const fb = $('button', ul); if (fb && BS.sel) fb.setAttribute('aria-pressed', 'true'); }
  drawDetail();
  const cF = list.filter(flagC).length, jF = list.filter(flagJ).length, mr = list.filter(r => r.ops.includes('MEANING_RENAME')).length;
  let t = list.length ? `Among these ${list.length} candidates the consensus flags ${pct(cF / list.length)} and the judge flags ${pct(jF / list.length)} at thresholds ${f2(TH.c)} and ${f2(TH.j)}.` : 'No candidates match.';
  if (list.length && (BS.cs === 'miss' || BS.cs === 'jwin')) t += ` ${pct(mr / Math.max(1, nE))} of the errors here carry a MEANING_RENAME operation, the error type an aligner can hide.`;
  if (list.length && BS.cs === 'fa') t += ` Mean sentence length is ${(list.reduce((s, r) => s + r.w, 0) / list.length).toFixed(1)} words, against ${(ROWS.reduce((s, r) => s + r.w, 0) / ROWS.length).toFixed(1)} over all candidates.`;
  $('#tk-browser').textContent = t;
}
function drawDetail() {
  const r = BS.sel, box = $('#b-detail');
  if (!r) { box.innerHTML = '<p class="small">Select a candidate.</p>'; return; }
  const s = SENT[r.s], c = sc(r, 'c_score_align'), j = sc(r, 'judge_cheap_disg');
  let fam = '';
  FAMS.forEach((f, i) => { const n = r.fm[2 * i], e = r.fm[2 * i + 1]; fam += `<div class="famrow"><span>${esc(f)}</span>${n ? `<span class="fambar" role="img" aria-label="${f}: ${e} of ${n} outputs equivalent"><i style="width:${100 * e / n}%"></i></span><span class="num">${e}/${n}</span>` : `<span class="small">${f === r.fam ? 'own family, excluded' : 'no output'}</span><span></span>`}</div>`; });
  const verdict = (flag, y) => flag === !!y ? '<span class="eqy">right</span>' : '<span class="eqn">wrong</span>';
  box.innerHTML = `<h4>Input sentence</h4><p style="font-size:1.05rem">“${esc(s.text)}”</p><p class="small">${r.w} words, ${r.nc} condition(s), ${esc(POPS[r.st].label)}. System: ${esc(r.sys)} (${esc(r.fam)}).</p>
  <div class="sbs"><div><h4>Candidate formula</h4><code class="fol">${esc(r.fol)}</code></div><div><h4>Reference (labelling only)</h4><code class="fol">${esc(s.ref)}</code></div></div>
  <div class="verd"><div><div class="small">Panel label</div><div>${tagOf(r.y ? 'ERROR' : 'CORRECT')}</div><div class="small">${r.ops.length ? 'Ops: ' + esc(r.ops.join(', ')) : ''} tier ${esc(r.tier)}</div></div>
  <div><div class="small">Consensus c_score_align</div><div class="v">${f3(c)}</div><div class="small">${flagC(r) ? 'flagged' : 'passed'} at ${f2(TH.c)}: ${verdict(flagC(r), r.y)}</div></div>
  <div><div class="small">Flash-lite judge, disguised</div><div class="v">${f2(j)}</div><div class="small">${flagJ(r) ? 'flagged' : 'passed'} at ${f2(TH.j)}: ${verdict(flagJ(r), r.y)}</div></div></div>
  <h4 style="margin-top:14px">Peer outputs Z3-equivalent to this candidate, by family</h4>${fam}`;
}

/* ---------- 3b. e / d by length ---------- */
const RULES = { MAJ: 'Majority of peers', PLUR: 'Plurality class', FAM2: 'Two or more families', FAMMAJ: 'Majority of families', MAJ_EXACT: 'Majority, no alignment' };
let RULE = 'MAJ';
function initED() { const seg = $('#rule-seg'); Object.keys(RULES).forEach(k => { const b = document.createElement('button'); b.type = 'button'; b.textContent = RULES[k]; b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', k === RULE); b.addEventListener('click', () => { RULE = k; $$('button', seg).forEach(x => x.setAttribute('aria-pressed', x.textContent === RULES[k])); drawED(); }); seg.appendChild(b); }); }
function drawED() {
  const cells = ['T1', 'T2', 'T3'].map(t => MECH.ed.find(x => x.dim === 'words_tercile' && x.cell === t && x.rule === RULE));
  cells.push(MECH.ed.find(x => x.dim === 'ALL' && x.rule === RULE));
  const names = ['Shortest third', 'Middle third', 'Longest third', 'All R_AB'];
  const host = $('#chart-ed'), W = Math.max(280, host.clientWidth || 500), H = 260, L = 40, R = 8, T = 10, B = 44;
  const svg = newSvg(host, W, H, 'Endorsement and divergence by sentence-length tercile');
  const y = v => T + (H - T - B) * (1 - v), gw = (W - L - R) / 4, bw = Math.min(34, gw * 0.3);
  [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1].forEach(t => { el('line', { class: 'gridl', x1: L, x2: W - R, y1: y(t), y2: y(t) }, svg); el('text', { x: L - 6, y: y(t) + 4, 'text-anchor': 'end', 'font-size': 11, fill: '#5a606a' }, svg, t); });
  el('text', { x: 12, y: T + (H - T - B) / 2, transform: `rotate(-90 12 ${T + (H - T - B) / 2})`, 'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': 11, fill: '#5a606a' }, svg, 'Rate (share of items)');
  cells.forEach((c, i) => {
    const cx = L + gw * i + gw / 2;
    el('text', { x: cx, y: H - B + 16, 'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': 11.5, fill: '#1c1e22' }, svg, names[i]);
    el('text', { x: cx, y: H - B + 30, 'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': 10.5, fill: '#5a606a' }, svg, `n ${c.n_err}/${c.n_cor}`);
    [['e', 'var(--base)', -1], ['d', 'var(--accent)', 1]].forEach(([k, colr, sgn]) => {
      const g = el('g', {}, svg), x0 = cx + (sgn < 0 ? -bw - 2 : 2), v = c[k], ci = c[k + '_ci'];
      el('rect', { class: 'hit', x: x0 - 2, y: T, width: bw + 4, height: H - T - B, fill: 'transparent' }, g);
      el('rect', { x: x0, y: y(v), width: bw, height: Math.max(1, y(0) - y(v)), fill: colr, rx: 2 }, g);
      el('line', { x1: x0 + bw / 2, x2: x0 + bw / 2, y1: y(ci[0]), y2: y(ci[1]), stroke: '#1c1e22', 'stroke-width': 1.3 }, g);
      el('text', { x: x0 + bw / 2, y: y(Math.max(v, ci[1])) - 4, 'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': 10.5 }, g, v.toFixed(2));
      bindMark(g, `<b>${names[i]}, ${RULES[RULE]}</b><br>${k === 'e' ? 'Endorsement e (errors endorsed)' : 'Divergence d (correct not endorsed)'}: ${f3(v)} [${f3(ci[0])}, ${f3(ci[1])}]<br>${c.n_err} ERROR / ${c.n_cor} CORRECT, ${c.n_sent} sentences<br>AUROC<sub>b</sub> = 1 − (e + d)/2 = ${f3(c.auroc_b)}`, `${names[i]} ${k} ${f3(v)}`);
    });
  });
  el('line', { x1: L, x2: W - R, y1: y(0), y2: y(0), stroke: '#c5c8c1' }, svg);
  const a = cells[0], b = cells[2];
  $('#tk-ed').textContent = `Rule “${RULES[RULE]}”: from the shortest to the longest third, d moves ${f3(a.d)} → ${f3(b.d)} and e moves ${f3(a.e)} → ${f3(b.e)}, so e + d changes by ${sg(b.e + b.d - a.e - a.d)} and binary AUROC falls from ${f3(a.auroc_b)} to ${f3(b.auroc_b)}. ${b.d > a.d ? 'Correct translations of long sentences stop agreeing with their peers.' : ''}`;
}

/* ---------- 3c. families ---------- */
const FSEL = new Set(FAMS);
function famScores() { return ROWS.map(r => { let n = 0, e = 0; FAMS.forEach((f, i) => { if (FSEL.has(f)) { n += r.fm[2 * i]; e += r.fm[2 * i + 1]; } }); return n >= 2 ? 1 - e / n : DR.neutral_c; }); }
function initFam() { const box = $('#fam-ck'); FAMS.forEach(f => { const l = document.createElement('label'); l.className = 'ck'; l.innerHTML = `<input type="checkbox" checked value="${f}"> ${f}`; l.querySelector('input').addEventListener('change', e => { if (e.target.checked) FSEL.add(f); else FSEL.delete(f); drawFam(); }); box.appendChild(l); }); }
function drawFam() {
  const vals = famScores(), idx = new Map(ROWS.map((r, i) => [r, i]));
  const auc = FSEL.size ? aurocStrat(ROWS, r => vals[idx.get(r)]) : null;
  const neutral = ROWS.filter((r, i) => { let n = 0; FAMS.forEach((f, k) => { if (FSEL.has(f)) n += r.fm[2 * k]; }); return n < 2; }).length;
  const j = aucFor('all', 'judge_cheap_disg');
  $('#fam-stat').innerHTML = `<div><div class="v">${FSEL.size}</div><div class="l">families in the pool</div></div><div><div class="v">${auc == null ? 'n/a' : f3(auc)}</div><div class="l">stratified AUROC, all R_AB</div></div><div><div class="v">${f3(j)}</div><div class="l">disguised judge baseline</div></div><div><div class="v">${neutral}</div><div class="l">rows with under 2 pooled peers (neutral score)</div></div>`;
  const missing = FAMS.filter(f => !FSEL.has(f));
  let t;
  if (!FSEL.size) t = 'With no families ticked there is no consensus to compute.';
  else if (!missing.length) t = `All eight families: the page's recomputation gives ${f3(auc)}, against the recorded ${f3(REC.recorded.c_score_align.strat)} (7 of 2,672 rows differ through a solver hash-seed effect documented in the audit).`;
  else t = `Without ${missing.join(', ')}, the consensus scores ${f3(auc)}, ${auc > j ? 'still above' : 'no longer above'} the disguised judge (${f3(j)}). The recorded curve reaches 97% of the full-pool AUROC at k = 3, but the longest tercile needs k = 5.`;
  $('#tk-k').textContent = t;
  drawK();
}
function drawK() {
  const host = $('#chart-k'), W = Math.max(280, host.clientWidth || 500), H = 230, L = 44, R = 12, T = 10, B = 40;
  const svg = newSvg(host, W, H, 'Recorded AUROC by number of peer families');
  const K = MECH.k_curve, x = k => L + (W - L - R) * (k - 1) / 6, y = v => T + (H - T - B) * (1 - (v - 0.5) / 0.35);
  [0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8].forEach(t => { el('line', { class: 'gridl', x1: L, x2: W - R, y1: y(t), y2: y(t) }, svg); el('text', { x: L - 6, y: y(t) + 4, 'text-anchor': 'end', 'font-size': 11, fill: '#5a606a' }, svg, t.toFixed(1)); });
  K.forEach(p => el('text', { x: x(p.k), y: H - B + 16, 'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': 11, fill: '#5a606a' }, svg, p.k));
  el('text', { x: (W + L) / 2, y: H - 6, 'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': 11, fill: '#5a606a' }, svg, 'Peer families k (random subsets, mean of 50)');
  el('text', { x: 12, y: T + (H - T - B) / 2, transform: `rotate(-90 12 ${T + (H - T - B) / 2})`, 'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': 11, fill: '#5a606a' }, svg, 'AUROC');
  [['auroc', '#1f5bb8', ''], ['T3', '#b8741f', '5 3']].forEach(([k, c, da]) => el('path', { d: K.map((p, i) => (i ? 'L' : 'M') + x(p.k) + ' ' + y(p[k])).join(' '), fill: 'none', stroke: c, 'stroke-width': 2.2, 'stroke-dasharray': da }, svg));
  K.forEach(p => {
    const g = el('g', {}, svg);
    el('rect', { class: 'hit', x: x(p.k) - 12, y: T, width: 24, height: H - T - B, fill: 'transparent' }, g);
    el('line', { x1: x(p.k), x2: x(p.k), y1: y(p.ci[0]), y2: y(p.ci[1]), stroke: '#1f5bb8', 'stroke-width': 1, opacity: .5 }, g);
    el('circle', { cx: x(p.k), cy: y(p.auroc), r: 4.5, fill: '#1f5bb8' }, g);
    el('circle', { cx: x(p.k), cy: y(p.T3), r: 4, fill: '#fff', stroke: '#b8741f', 'stroke-width': 2 }, g);
    bindMark(g, `<b>k = ${p.k} families</b><br>All sentences: ${f3(p.auroc)} [${f3(p.ci[0])}, ${f3(p.ci[1])}]<br>Longest tercile T3: ${f3(p.T3)}<br>Generation cost $${p.usd.toFixed(5)} per sentence`, `k ${p.k}: AUROC ${f3(p.auroc)}, longest tercile ${f3(p.T3)}`);
  });
  if (FSEL.size >= 1 && FSEL.size <= 7) { const kk = FSEL.size; el('line', { x1: x(kk), x2: x(kk), y1: T, y2: H - B, stroke: '#1c1e22', 'stroke-dasharray': '2 3' }, svg); el('text', { x: x(kk) + 4, y: T + 10, 'font-size': 11 }, svg, 'your k'); }
}

/* ---------- 4. try it ---------- */
let TPOP = 'all';
function rocPts(rows, m) {
  const pts = rows.map(r => [sc(r, m), r.y]).sort((a, b) => b[0] - a[0]);
  const P = pts.filter(p => p[1]).length, N = pts.length - P; let tp = 0, fp = 0; const out = [[0, 0]];
  for (let i = 0; i < pts.length; i++) { if (pts[i][1]) tp++; else fp++; if (i === pts.length - 1 || pts[i + 1][0] !== pts[i][0]) out.push([fp / N, tp / P]); }
  return out;
}
function opPoint(rows, m, t) { let tp = 0, fp = 0, P = 0, N = 0; rows.forEach(r => { const f = sc(r, m) >= t - 1e-9; if (r.y) { P++; if (f) tp++; } else { N++; if (f) fp++; } }); return { rec: tp / P, fa: fp / N, flagged: tp + fp, P, N }; }
function initTry() {
  const s = $('#t-pop'); s.innerHTML = Object.keys(POPS).map(k => `<option value="${k}">${POPS[k].label}</option>`).join('');

The rename table, the k-curve, the tercile e/d numbers (+0.356) and the confirmation cells also match the paper. The page is 1.36 MB with no external assets.

**What's on the page:**
- **The finding:** a bar chart of stratified AUROC for 13 metrics. You can switch between six populations and toggle metric groups; the judge baseline is always shown. On short control sentences it correctly shows the judge ahead.
- **How it works:** a 5-stage stepper over two real sentences, with the full peer outputs and pairwise solver verdicts. You can pick any candidate, and the page recomputes its score from the recorded verdicts and shows it matches the stored value. The second sentence shows the failure case, where peers agree with the errors.
- **Explore the evidence:**
  - An item browser over all 2,686 candidates, with filters for cases like "errors the consensus endorses". The detail panel puts the candidate formula beside the reference.
  - A length chart with a selector for the voting rule.
  - Family checkboxes that re-score every row live from the solver matrix.
- **Try it:** threshold sliders with ROC curves and a button that gives the judge the same false-alarm rate as the consensus, so recall can be compared fairly.
- **Where it fails:** the rename tradeoff, recall per error type, the confirmation table, and the paper's limitations.
- **Footer:** all three links, where each view's data comes from, a glossary of 18 terms with tooltips, and the citation.

**Where the page differs from the paper:**
- **Nano judge model:** the paper calls it Gemini Flash 2.0, but the run's data shows gpt-4.1-nano. I label it only "nano judge".
- **Panel:** the paper calls it an expert panel, but the dataset describes an LLM panel. I say only "panel labels".
- **Benchmark gold:** one stepper row is the benchmark's original gold formula run as a system. I label it that way and show its panel label rather than calling it the reference, because in the second example that gold is labelled ERROR.

**Paper figures:** none of the three are on the page. All three are data plots that the page redraws from the data.

In `index.html` I added only the two "Explore the website" links, in the hero and the footer. I didn't touch the folder's README or manifest, since the task said to change nothing else. The structured output is in `.terminal_claude_agent_struct_out.json`.
